extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / anabelian geometry (readers of Mochizuki's IUT papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and technical criteria for constructing and interpreting cyclotomic-rigidity isomorphisms, related multiradial/uniradial functors, and associated group-theoretic algorithms in the context of Inter-Universal Teichmüller Theory (IUT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coricity of O× and inclusion of MLF-Galois TCG-pair in coric data
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of the 'coricity of O×' (IUTchI, Corollary 3.7, (iii)), in addition to G it is possible to take the underlying MLF-Galois TCG-pair of 'G ⨯ O×(G)' to be part of one's coric data, up to an (Aut(G), Γ (= Z×))-indeterminacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep in mind the Aut(G)- vs Γ-indeterminacy decomposition; the p-adic portion of the Γ-indeterminacy cannot be subsumed into Aut(G)-indeterminacy (Remark 1.8.1). This choice amounts to working with 'G ⨯ O×(G)' only up to these indeterminacies; record the indeterminacy explicitly when treating such coric data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work with O×μ (quotient by torsion) for multiradial functors
rubrics_metrics.description: To construct multiradially defined functors that are crucial in the theory, one must form the quotient of 'O×(−)' by its torsion subgroup 'Oμ(−)', i.e., work with 'O×μ(−)' rather than 'O×(−)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on the underlying ind-topological module with topological group action; pass to O×μ to obtain the right form of coric data for multiradial constructions (cf. Corollary 1.10/1.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with natural maps induces propagated indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: Compatibility with respect to the natural maps Ogp(G) ← O×(G) → O×μ(G) implies that the (Aut(G), Γ)-indeterminacy on 'G ⨯ O×μ(G)' induces corresponding (Aut(G), Γ)-indeterminacies on 'G ⨯ O×(G)' and 'G ⨯ Ogp(G)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When specifying coric data, track how indeterminacies on one part (e.g., O×μ) force indeterminacies elsewhere. View Γ-indeterminacy on Ogp(G) as indeterminacy in specifying the submonoid O(G) ⊆ Ogp(G). These induced 'orbits' appear in subsequent corollaries (e.g., Corollary 1.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow post-anabelian input to cyclotomic rigidity algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: The cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism algorithms (Corollaries 1.10, 1.11) are obtained by composing group-theoretic construction algorithms with algorithms whose input is 'post-anabelian' (i.e., objects arising after forgetting anabelian structure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design algorithms so their inputs need not arise from a group-theoretic construction algorithm; they should accept post-anabelian data such as systems of mono-theta environments or MLF-Galois TM-pairs, and record the induced indeterminacies/orbits that this entails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish strict cyclotomic rigidity from multiradial rigidity with indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary 1.10 exhibits 'strict cyclotomic rigidity' (triviality of the homomorphism relating the cyclotomic portion of O(−) to coric data O×μ(−)); by contrast Corollary 1.11 has substantial indeterminacies due to nontrivial relationships between input data and coric data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a situation, check whether the relevant homomorphism is trivial (strict rigidity) or nontrivial (expect orbits/indeterminacies). This distinction affects whether outputs are label-independent or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of reconstruction algorithm matters (not just existence)
rubrics_metrics.description: In reconstruction contexts (e.g., group-theoretic reconstruction algorithms), sometimes not only the existence of 'some' reconstruction algorithm, but also the specific content/definition of the reconstruction algorithm is crucial for the theory's development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to algorithmic choices and normalizations; different reconstruction algorithms can produce different indeterminacies or data splittings that materially affect downstream constructions (cf. Example 3.5 of IUTchIV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate (Aut(G),Γ)-indeterminacy via uniradial environments
rubrics_metrics.description: One can eliminate the (Aut(G), Γ)-indeterminacy of Corollary 1.11 by working with uniradially defined functors (replace 'G ⨯ O(G)' by Π ⨯ MTM(Π) and G by Π/Δ, working in the corresponding uniradial environment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If indeterminacy is problematic, consider passing to an appropriate uniradial environment; this may replace multiradial definitions with uniradial ones that remove the stated indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow algorithms to accept data from Frobenioid monoid/rational function portions
rubrics_metrics.description: We wish cyclotomic rigidity algorithms whose input is post-anabelian so they can apply to input data that does not arise from a group-theoretic construction algorithm — for example, data arising from the divisor and rational-function monoid portion of a Frobenioid (Proposition 1.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the algorithms to accept monoidal data (e.g., from Frobenioids) and be prepared to relate different cyclotomes via intermediate constructions, noting resulting indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for passing through intermediate cyclotomes and induced indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: To relate exterior cyclotome of a mono-theta environment (Corollary 1.10) to the cyclotome μZ(O×(G)) of Corollary 1.11, one must pass through the cyclotome (l · ΔΘ)(Π) applying cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms, which in Corollary 1.11 produces indeterminacies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relating cyclotomes, record intermediate steps and the indeterminacies introduced at each transition; do not assume direct identification without analyzing intermediate passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain splitting/decoupling into radial (label-dependent) and coric (label-independent) components
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary 1.10 yields a splitting (decoupling) that separates the 'purely radial data' (label-dependent) from the 'purely coric data' constituted by O×μ(−), resulting in output data equipped with both label-dependent and label-independent components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to identify splittings that confine label-dependence to the radial component while preserving a label-independent coric part; this is significant for eliminating unwanted label-dependent data in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulate kernels and related data as (multi)radially defined functors
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural surjections (e.g., H^1(G, μZ(G)) → Z) constructed functorially imply that the corresponding kernel (e.g., O×k) may be formulated as a corically and hence as a multiradially defined functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, express structural objects (kernels of natural surjections, submodules) as multi/uniradial functors; this clarifies their behavior under indeterminacies and Galois actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial algorithm assigning pointed inversion automorphisms (ι, D)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a functorial group-theoretic algorithm Π ↦ {(ι, D)}(Π) assigning to a topological group Π a collection of pairs (ι, D), where ι is a ΔY(Π)-outer automorphism of ΠY(Π) and D is a ΔY(Π)-conjugacy class of closed subgroups; these are 'pointed inversion automorphisms'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing invariants/splittings, build such functorial assignments; they are essential for defining ι-invariants and for producing the splittings in (†μθ)(Π).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct splittings via restriction to conjugacy-class subgroups and cyclotomic rigidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction to the subgroup D associated to a pointed inversion automorphism gives a commutative diagram whose inverse images of torsion submodules yield ∞θ(Π)^ι and related objects, producing functorial algorithms for constructing splittings (†μθ)(Π).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement the restriction-to-D step and use the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism to obtain bijections and identify torsion-invariant submodules; these give the desired direct-product decompositions in quotients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify multiradiality via fullness/surjectivity of radial onto coric data
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiradiality amounts to a sort of 'surjectivity' (fullness condition) of the radial data onto the coric data; splittings (†μθ)(Π) reflect a decomposition of this surjection into radial and coric components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To claim multiradiality, check the fullness condition (e.g., Example 1.7 (ii),(v)); demonstrate that radial data maps onto coric data up to the stated indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalize étale theta functions by fixing values at points over 2-torsion to ensure multiradiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The functorial algorithm for θ(Π) up to μ2l-indeterminacy is achieved by normalizing étale theta functions of 'standard type' by requiring their values at points lying over the 2-torsion point μ− be ∈ μ2l; this normalization is key to multiradiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When normalizing theta functions, require those evaluations at chosen 2-torsion lifts lie in μ2l to guarantee the functorial construction is multiradial; record the decomposition groups used in reconstruction (elliptic cuspidalizations, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid normalizations depending on specific arithmetic holomorphic structures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the normalization requires theta-values that depend on the ring structure relative to some specific Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater (e.g., requiring a theta-value equal to 2 = 1+1), the normalization will fail to give a multiradially defined functor and only yield a uniradially defined functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not impose normalizations that reference data tied to a particular arithmetic holomorphic structure; such choices introduce unwanted label-dependence and break multiradiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain indeterminacy bounded by μ for log-shell applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For log-shell theory (to be used in later papers), having splittings only up to a μ-indeterminacy is acceptable; a larger indeterminacy (e.g., subgroup generated by 2 and its Aut(G)-conjugates) would force inconsistent quotienting of O×μ(G) and is unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing data for log-shell theory, ensure the indeterminacy is no larger than the μ subgroup; otherwise the image of the log-shell will only be well-defined in an unacceptable quotient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require evaluation algorithms be compatible with forming Kummer classes and extend to coverings (Galois evaluation principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'mysterious' evaluation algorithm (abstract theta function → theta values) should be compatible with forming Kummer classes by extracting N-th roots and should extend to coverings on both input and output; this functorial Galois compatibility (principle of Galois evaluation) implies the algorithm arises from a section G → ΠY(Π).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impose functoriality under Galois groups and compatibility with Kummer constructions; if satisfied, one may conclude the evaluation is group-theoretic (arises from a continuous section), aligning with expectations from the Section Conjecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer theta-evaluation algorithms that use only the topological group Π as input
rubrics_metrics.description: The theta-evaluation functorial algorithm of Corollary 1.12 (ii), given by restriction to decomposition groups associated to μ−, involves only the topological group Π as input — a crucial property for combining with log-shell theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design evaluation algorithms to be purely group-theoretic (input = Π) whenever possible, as this facilitates later combination with log-shells and supports Section-Conjecture-type interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruct tempered-covering diagrams functorially from Πtp_X
rubrics_metrics.description: The diagram of tempered fundamental groups and their open-subgroup relations (Proposition 2.1) can be reconstructed via a functorial group-theoretic algorithm from the temp-slim topological group Πtp_Xv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working with tempered coverings and related open-injection diagrams, use the cited functorial reconstruction results ([EtTh], [SemiAnbd]) to rebuild the diagram from the topological group data; this ensures compatibility with subsequent group-theoretic algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle conjugate synchronization and conjugacy indeterminacies carefully in theta-evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic theta-evaluation depends on a careful analysis of conjugate synchronization (synchronizing conjugates of copies of objects attached to the absolute Galois group at evaluation points) and computation of conjugacy indeterminacies arising from closed subgroups of topological groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly analyze conjugate synchronization issues and compute resulting conjugacy indeterminacies (see Corollaries 2.4, 2.5). This is necessary for correct Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation with a single basepoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure constructions remain valid for strictly local data where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Many constructions in §2 are valid for strictly local data (i.e., that which does not arise from global number-field data); nevertheless, for compatibility reasons with IUTchI the exposition keeps the global-local notation consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying the constructions, verify they hold in the strictly local context if needed, and adapt notation and compatibility checks when linking local constructions to global IUT settings.
